subject: Dam Maintenance Letter - Jack Harris
bodyText:
Hello,

Jack Harris is sending out a letter requesting signatures to approve future maintenance costs for the dam.

Please do not sign this document until Steve has had the opportunity to review and approve it.

Thank you for your cooperation.

Thanks,

Mark

subject: Fwd: Dam Litigation Status Report
bodyText:
Please see below for the current status report.

Also, please note that the letters sent to some members regarding the lawsuit and dam maintenance were sent in error. They were not intended to be distributed to members of our group.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

> Begin forwarded message:
>
> From: "Stephen E. Chappelear" <sechappelear@eastmansmith.com>
> Subject: Dam Litigation Status Report
> Date: July 10, 2026 at 11:23:23 EDT
> To: Mark A Long <mark@mdsaholdings.com>
>
> Mark,
>
> This will summarize the telephone status conference held with Judge Wetzel on June 26, 2026.
>
> Jack Harris reported that the construction work for remediation of the dam is on schedule and actually two days ahead of schedule. He said that they expect to have the work completed by the end of July, except for seeding, which will hold off until September.
>
> He reported that he has been reaching out to homeowners who are not part of a homeowners association to get written consents. So far he has received just one "no." He also said that he has reached out to homeowner association presidents to get backing for a maintenance plan. He said that he will have an exact figure for how much the maintenance will be.
>
> The attorney for the Receiver said that the day before she had filed a Notice of Amendment concerning the Declarations. She said that she was finalizing the draft bylaws.
>
> I said that we were expecting the proposed Amendment weeks ago, because in the last status report, the attorney said that it would be submitted in the coming week. I said that we had not had an opportunity to study the draft Amendment, and wanted to have adequate time to do that. The court agreed.
>
> The former City Engineer (Brian Ball) has left the City. Quintin Platt is the acting City Engineer and was on the call.
>
> Mr. Harris said that he has made a calculation regarding the maintenance costs, and that has been approved by the City Engineer. He now has to calculate how many people will pay and noted that there are many moving parts. He said that he would have a report the next month.
>
> I asked that the next status conference be moved back a week to August 7. There was no objection, and the court agreed.
>
> Mr. Harris mentioned that the City submits a weekly written report to him. I asked that copies of these be given to counsel, and the court agreed.
>
> Mr. Harris said that the contractor has been pulling clay from a borrow site about a mile away and taking topsoil back to that site. This is resulting in a cost savings.
>
> Regarding maintenance costs, I said that it would be beneficial to everyone if the Receiver could share with us what the anticipated maintenance costs will be, and for what. The attorney for the Receiver agreed to provide that to us. I said that the sooner that is done, the better. As of today, I have not received anything. I have sent a follow up request to the attorney.
>
> Please let me know if you have any questions.
>
> Steve

subject: Re: Dam Litigation Status Report
bodyText:
Mark,

       I have now received 3 (identical) letters from Jack Harris asking for a signature on the maintenance agreement. I have not signed any of those agreements.

        Just to be clear (I know it's obvious but it doesn't hurt to ask):
1. In a previous email, you said to hold off signing until Steve could review the agreement.
2. The current email says this agreement is only intended for those OUTSDIDE the dam litigation group (but presumably within the watershed of the lake).

So my conclusion is that we (the dam litigation group) don't have to wait for a review, since this agreement should not have been sent to us in the first place. So obviously do not sign it.

Is that about right?

Thanks,
Mike

[quoted original message from Mark Long, "Fwd: Dam Litigation Status Report", July 11 2026, and forwarded status report from Stephen E. Chappelear dated July 10 2026 - see prior message in thread for full text]

subject: RE: Dam Litigation Status Report
bodyText:
Mike,

I did review the consent letter and immediately contacted the attorney for the Receiver, demanding information about why this was sent out, protesting it having been sent without it being sent to the attorney, and posing a number of questions about the purpose of the consent form.

That attorney was on vacation, but still wrote and said he did not know why it was sent to our clients, that it was not supposed to have been, and said he would have it checked it out.

I later heard from another attorney in his office who confirmed that it should not have been sent to any of you. It was only supposed to go to homeowners in the area who are not part of an HOA.

So, you are correct. You should NOT SIGN the consent form, if you received one.

Steve

subject: Re: Eastman & Smith, Ltd. - RETAINER REPLENISHMENT DUE BY SEPTEMBER 25, 202 [ES-LEGAL.FID2347402]
bodyText:
Good Evening All,

I have attached an updated KCCD Status Summary for your review.

I do not believe a strategy meeting is necessary at this point and, in fact, it could potentially complicate our current representation. The strategy we have followed to date has produced the results we want: the dam has been repaired, no additional contingency funds were required, and a long-term maintenance plan with proposed fees is now on the table.

We have also just completed approximately two months of construction activity that required significant participation from our attorney. Given that level of activity, it is not surprising that the legal funds we contributed in July have been exhausted.

We are very close to bringing this matter to a conclusion. Changing strategies at this stage is more likely to slow our progress than improve the outcome.

Please review the attached summary. At this point, what we need most is consensus or feedback on the proposed ongoing maintenance assessment, as well as consensus on the proposed one-time vegetation assessment.

Please provide your feedback or contact me with any questions.

Thanks,

Mark

[quoted original retainer replenishment message from Juli R. McCafferty - see prior message in thread]

I do not believe a strategy meeting is necessary at this point and, in fact, it could potentially complicate our current representation. We have also just completed approximately two months of construction activity that required significant participation from our attorney. Given that level of activity, it is not surprising that the legal funds we contributed in July have been exhausted.

We are very close to bringing this matter to a conclusion. Changing strategies at this stage is more likely to slow our progress than improve the outcome.

subject: Re: Eastman & Smith, Ltd. - RETAINER REPLENISHMENT DUE BY SEPTEMBER 25, 202
bodyText:
Mark,
Again thanks for your work on this. I do see light at the end of the tunnel and I don't think it's a train.

Several things: 1. What would/did we approve the change to the Development Restrictions proposed by the receiver? Changing the name of the HOA materially changes the document. It changes the status of the HOA from a non-owner if the land to an owner. The receiver has no standing to make changes to the document. The land in the HOA is not part of the our respective subdivisions. The document itself requires 75 percent of the land owners to approve the cancellation of the restrictions and is silent on a percentage to amend. In the absence of a percentage I would assume 75 percent. And this is for the individual subdivision not the combination of the two. The judge may believe that the association should be landowners but the document clearly state the developer is the owner at the time of filing. 2. Let's treat all assessments the same way. If land concentration is a factor for monthly assessments then let's make lake front property and non lake front property variable in the extra clean up of the property. Let's start with lake front properties are assessed 50% of the cost and non lake front properties the other 50%. The lake front can divide their amount by units, linear feet, or any other formula the desire. Non lake front can simply divide by the number of properties. I know it's only $175 at most for this work as proposed but if feel like we have given at every turn and have not received any concessions. 3. Is it possible to get an independent evaluation of annual maintenance and long term maintenance of the property? The city is going to recommend a Cadillac when maybe there is a Chevy solution. They don't care it's not their money. And the more they collect in assessment the more they send to their general fund for Administrative charges. 4. The city has been collecting $6 a month for years, and will continue to collect it, from each property in the group year they do recommend using any of that in the storm water utility maintenance solution.

Now that the dam work is completed our strategy must be to get us out of the lawsuit, have it dismissed with prejudice and make sure we are not liable for any other party's legal fees. I am sick and tired of the judge holding us hostage when we, as individuals, have no business being in the lawsuit.

Please let me know your thoughts.
Jesse

subject: Termination of Legal Representation
bodyText:
This message is to advise you that our law firm will no longer be representing any of you in the case now pending in the Knox County Court of Common Pleas involving the Knox Cattle Dam. We will be filing a motion with the court to withdraw as your legal counsel.

We have come to this point primarily because I have been unable to get critical information and direction from representatives of the group on important issues, including the assessments for ongoing maintenance of the property where the dam and lakes are, the method and cost for vegetation clearing, dues for the HOA, governance of the HOA, potential officers and directors of the HOA, and our strategy for the remainder of the case.

Our law firm is unable to provide effective legal representation without information and direction from our clients.

My reasonable expectation is that this situation will not improve in the near term, but will in fact become even worse. I have recently learned that one of the representatives is moving out of state in the next month, and the other will no longer be a part of the group and no longer wishes to have us serve as his legal counsel. And, I am not seeing anyone else in the group take an interest in assuming that role, or providing necessary information.

Whether you like the lawsuit or not, or being sued, or having to pay legal fees, or the dam, or the lake, or your neighbors, or the HOA, there are realities that cannot be ignored, and the lawsuit is not going away by simply wishing it were so. We cannot do our job as your legal counsel if you do not participate in the process.

I understand that many of you are frustrated and annoyed with having been sued, and having to spend money on legal fees on a case you would prefer was not there. Some original members of the group have dropped out. I have heard from several more that they want to drop legal representation as well.

Whether this is wise or not for these individuals is not my call to make, or whether it is fair to the remaining members of the group to take on a larger proportion of the legal fees while allowing others to get the indirect benefit of legal work without contributing to the expense.

Given that some people in the group are telling us that they are unwilling to pay our law firm its fees for continued representation, that presents a second reason for us to terminate our representation. This is a breach of our engagement letter.

I do strongly believe that you should each have legal counsel in this case, and my strong recommendation is that you each take immediate steps to retain substitute legal counsel as soon as possible.

Because we will no longer be representing you, you do not need to pay the $800 we recently requested to replenish the retainer fund. If you have already sent that payment in, it will be refunded to you.

Here are some important things for your new legal counsel to address, quickly.

  1. On September 23, 2024, Judge Wetzel issued his Decision and Entry on Motions for Partial Summary Judgment. On page 7, he held that the Phase VII and VIII lot owners are bound by the Declaration of Building and Development Restrictions. See also, pages 18-24. On page 24, the court stated, "Because the Declaration of Restrictions are [sic] enforceable against the Developer, Mullins Bros., and the respective lot owners, it is incumbent upon these parties to comply with the Declaration of Restrictions, and this Court will enforce the Declaration of Restrictions by further orders of this Court. Each party is enjoined from attempting or adopting any amendment or modifications of the Declaration of Restrictions without further order of this Court."
  2. Paragraph 4(B) of the Declarations, as recently amended, states, "Developer shall require the owners of all lots to become members of an Ohio non-profit corporation known as the Landings Property Owners Association, Inc. This corporation shall have the sole and exclusive control of the lake located on the land of the Developer and shall be responsible for its care and maintenance."
  3. In the Interim Order for Appointment of Receiver for the Landings Property Owners Association, Inc. filed October 4, 2024, Judge Wetzel stated, on pages 5 and 6, that the Receiver was ordered to: "6. Work with the Defendant Mullins Bros., and with the defendants Phase VII and Phase VIII Lot Owners, to organize and to establish rules and regulations for the governance and the operations of a homeowners association in accordance with the Ohio Revised Code, and pursuant to the Declarations of Building and Development Restrictions which this Court has found are binding upon Mullins Bros. and the Phase VII and Phase VIII Lot owners, and to achieve full compliance with and enforcement of those Declarations of Building and Development Restrictions. 7. Determine needed assessments on the Phase VII and Phase VIII Lot Owners pursuant to the Declarations of Building and Development Restrictions in order to comply with the terms of this Order, and work with the City to implement a mechanism to levy and collect those assessments..."
  4. Therefore, there IS an HOA, which is the Landings Property Owners Association, Inc., and ALL lot owners in Phases VII and VIII are members of it, whether they like it or not, and the Receiver WILL impose rules and regulations for the governance of the HOA if the lot owners do not participate and cooperate, which makes no sense at all for the lot owners. I think the lot owners should pick their own rules and regulations, but this requires the lot owners to participate in the process, which I have yet to see anyone willing to do.
  5. The Receiver has proposed Bylaws for the HOA. I requested revisions. The Receiver responded. I have communicated those to the group's representatives. The Receiver is awaiting information from the group about the Bylaws, and the expenses undergone by the former HOA, and the anticipated expenses for the new HOA, and the dues for the HOA. The Receiver will also want to know, very soon, who from the neighborhood will be the directors and officers of the new HOA.
  6. The Receiver has obtained an estimate of $45,000 to remove vegetation in the lake area, and wants to do a one-time assessment to cover this cost. This raises several issues. Is that estimate reasonable? Could the work be done by someone else for less? Does all of the work in the estimate need to be done? Who benefits from this work being done? Who does not? Who is asking for this work to be done? How should the cost be allocated? Should those individuals living closest to the lakes pay more (or all)?
  7. The Receiver has worked with the City of Mount Vernon to determine a monthly assessment to cover this cost of future maintenance of the lakes, including seeding and mulching, topsoil, mowing, herbicide application, engineering, dewatering, dredging, mulching, inspections, and other items. This raises several issues. Are the numbers reasonable? Could the work be done by someone else for less? Does all of the work in the estimate need to be done? Who benefits from this work being done? Who does not? How should the cost be allocated? Should those individuals living closest to the lakes pay more (or all)? What is the interplay between the $6/month assessment you are paying now and this new assessment?
  8. The Receiver's attorney will be filing a motion soon asking the court to approve assessments for vegetation removal and future maintenance. A written response will be due two weeks later with the court. The Receiver is not a fiduciary with any duties to the lot owners. He has shown that he is much more interested in pleasing officials of the City of Mount Vernon, than the lot owners. He is not acting in the best interests of the lot owners. If you rely upon him, you do so at your peril.
  9. There are monthly status calls with the Judge on the last Friday of each month, at 11:00 a.m. The next one is September 25, 2026. Call 1-646-931-3860; Participant PIN: 873 5606 7080#
  10. There are multiple pending issues in the lawsuit, which I expect the court to return to very soon, now that the dam remediation work has been completed within the available federal funds, and the Receiver is working through the HOA governance process, and the assessments. In the September 23, 2024 Decision and Entry on Motions for Partial Summary Judgment, on page 27, Judge Wetzel stated, "Any other matters remaining unresolved by this Decision and Entry on the pending motions for summary judgment, and any outstanding claims raised by the parties in their pleadings which are not yet resolved will be determined at trial or upon further hearing. A number of claims remain outstanding and unresolved, such as cross-party claims for indemnity and contribution, injunctive relief, violations of the Water Pollution Control Act, and breach of contract of the terms of the Declarations of Restrictions, and any other claims for breach of contract and damages."

I wish you all the best.

EASTMAN & SMITH

Subject: Phase VII & VIII – Continued Legal Representation

Good Day,

Despite Eastman & Smith's decision to withdraw, there remains a significant group of owners who have indicated that they do not wish to proceed without legal counsel. The following owners/households have expressed their intent to maintain representation:

Mark & Denise Long
Ken & Andrea Belcher
Derk & Anita Demaree
Jan & Ed Cosby
James & Cindy Kosmos
Marcello & Peggy Codispoti
Peggy Snow
Mark Cochran / Cochran Keystone Trust
Andreas & Patty Giakoumas
Jeff & Joy (Rachel) Strickland
Richard Littleton / Household
Michael Ulrey
Tim & Dianne Williams
Mark Tuel
Deborah Hamilton
Jeanne Mullendore
Matthew Snow / Snow Household
Jesse & Jane Marlow
Alexander & Marcia Varughese
Diane Goodrich
Kenneth & Mary Rhoades
This represents 21 participating households/entries and more than 20 individual property owners who wish to maintain legal representation.

Given Eastman & Smith's withdrawal, we will now need to secure substitute counsel for this group. Our preference would be to explore representation with an attorney already involved in the existing litigation, provided there are no conflicts that would prevent such representation. An attorney already participating in the case would be familiar with its history, the parties, the Receiver, and the matters presently before the Court. This should substantially reduce the learning curve and associated legal expense.

The intent of this group is not to interfere with the Board's ability to conduct normal HOA business. Rather, the objective is to maintain independent legal representation for those owners who want it while the remaining litigation is brought to conclusion. HOA matters can continue through the appropriate HOA process, while counsel can focus on protecting the represented owners' interests in the litigation and pursuing an appropriate path toward dismissal and finality.

With the upcoming September 25 status conference, identifying replacement counsel should be treated as a priority.

If the Board or any member is aware of counsel already participating in this case who may be willing and able to represent this group, I would appreciate those recommendations so that we can begin those discussions promptly.

Thank you,

Mark Long
